sourceActivityComparison.repair: Existing Rich V2 omitted this exact visual comparison; independent SVG is an analogue for classification, not a reconstruction of A-D. Source-task parity remains open.

sourceActivityComparison.original: Drag vertices, record other angle/side measures; compare Jada single 75° angle, Andre 75° and 45°, Lin two angles and one 5-cm side.

sourceActivityComparison.original: Explore 60°/60° and side 4 cm (one shape); 90°/90° and side 4 cm (none); 60°/90° and side 4 cm (several if which side is unspecified), with learner-drawn evidence.

one.congruentReason: All sides 4 cm; rotation or reflection does not create a new triangle.

none.why: Perpendicular rays through distinct endpoints of a common base are parallel and cannot intersect to form a third triangle vertex.

multiple.why: Same two angles, but the 4 cm side occupies a different corresponding position.

learnerTask: Use ruler and protractor, or independently implemented angle controls, to draw triangles using each source condition. Record original point/ray measurements and label which side is 4 cm. Show two noncongruent triangles for the unspecified 60°/90°/4 cm case; explain why two right-angle rays cannot form a triangle, and demonstrate congruence of equilateral 4 cm constructions. Draw more than one triangle for single 75° or 75°/45° alone and compare sizes. Submit drawings and explanation for teacher review.

criteria.description: Construct and accurately label triangle/ray diagrams for 60/60/4, 90/90/4 and 60/90/4 cases using proper measurement and units.
Distinguish one equilateral congruence class, impossible two-right-angle condition and multiple noncongruent right-triangle sizes; justify with drawings.
Show that 75° and 75°/45° angle-only conditions allow scaled copies, but fixing a corresponding 5-cm side removes scale freedom.
Document student-made measurements, label corresponding side placement and explain reasoning in writing/orally; reject malformed or unmeasured sketches.
